description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number for five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROMEO—across a range of co-occurrence numbers from $10^1$ to $10^3$. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 60 to 80. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black, circle), MEND (brown, diamond), FT (blue, triangle), MEMIT (purple, pentagon), and ROMEO (green, square). All five lines show a general upward trend, indicating that accuracy increases as the co-occurrence number increases. At a co-occurrence number of $10^1$, the Base method has the lowest accuracy at approximately 65%, while ROMEO has the highest at about 74%. At $10^3$, the Base method reaches an accuracy of approximately 71%, while ROMEO reaches the highest accuracy of about 81%. The other methods follow a similar pattern, with ROMEO consistently achieving the highest accuracy and Base the lowest across all co-occurrence numbers.
